links.outcome: Reliability of AI cephalometric tracing for clinical use without human oversight
links.effect: High concordance with computer-assisted manual tracing overall, but not sufficiently reliable in clinical practice without human oversight; Mthd significantly affected 62 of 85 measurements.
links.quote: Conclusion Although cephalometric landmark detection and measurements from AudaxCeph, OrthoDx, and WebCeph show high concordance with computer-assisted manual tracing, their use in clinical practice is not sufficiently reliable without human oversight.

links.outcome: Whether manual correction of automated tracings removes clinically unacceptable differences
links.effect: Semi-automated (manually corrected) modes compared with fully automated; U1-NA° and U1-L1° remained clinically unacceptable across all AI programs even after researcher intervention.
links.quote: U1-NA° and U1-L1° showed clinically unacceptable differences from RV across all AI programs, even after researcher intervention.
